**Evaluating allocation options**

I have three allocation options to discuss. For Option 1, the stability-first approach allocates 50% to camps, 20% to border, 20% to host communities, and 10% to local visibility projects. This secures camp gains but risks neglecting the acute needs of newly displaced groups. Option 2 focuses on needs rebalance, giving 30% to camps, 40% to border, and so on.
**Recommending balanced allocation**

For Option 3, which I recommend, I suggest a balanced, local-led approach: 30% to camps, 25% to border, 25% to host communities, and 20% to local visibility projects. This option targets the needs of border and minority populations while channeling resources effectively through national partners to maintain political support and enhance sustainability. rounds.response:
Given the comfortable but finite buffer, trade‑offs remain among four priorities (long‑standing camps, border/newly displaced/minorities, central/peri‑urban host communities, and channeling funds through national/local partners and donor‑visible urban projects); below are three concrete allocation options (percent of total envelope) with principal trade‑offs.  
Option 1 — Stability‑first: Camps 50%, Border 20%, Host 20%, Local/visibility 10%; secures camp gains and donor confidence but risks worsening acute needs and protection gaps among newly displaced minorities and border areas.  
Option 2 — Needs‑rebalancing: Camps 30%, Border 40%, Host 20%, Local/visibility 10%; prioritizes the most precarious new arrivals and protection‑scarce groups but will be perceived as deprioritizing long‑standing camp commitments and may strain camp operations.  
Option 3 — Balanced, local‑led (my recommended): Camps 30%, Border 25%, Host 25%, Local/visibility 20%; this scales up assistance for border/minority caseloads and host communities while substantially channeling resources through national partners and donor‑visible urban projects to protect sustainability and political support.  
For any option, ring‑fence a 10% rapid‑response contingency for sudden shocks and conduct monthly indicator‑based reviews (food security, malnutrition, protection) to reallocate funds quickly and limit unfair outcomes.
